title: Hybrid Token Batcher: KV Fragmentation Mitigation & Memory-Aware Scheduling for Mixed-Length Workloads
creator: Drew Chen
description: Problem: mixed prompt/response length workloads create adversarial patterns for our continuous batching scheduler: long-context requests inflate per-request KV footprint and cause KV memory fragmentation, which reduces effective GPU capacity and causes head-of-line blocking. Goal: implement a 'hybrid token batcher' that schedules by an estimated KV-memory footprint (not just token count), reduces KV fragmentation via allocation/coalescing heuristics, and preserves p95 latency SLOs while improving tail throughput and lowering OOM events.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler groups requests by estimated KV footprint and target batch footprint with <=10% p95 latency regression compared to baseline on 1k QPS mixed-length trace
End-to-end KV memory fragmentation metric improves (compaction gap reduced) by >=35% on replayed production traces
GPU OOMs related to KV allocations reduced to zero for the tested traces and autoscaling thresholds remain stable
Throughput (tokens/sec) improves by >=8% on long-tail heavy workloads compared to current continuous batcher
Features gated behind a runtime flag and rolloutable by customer/region; unit + integration tests in CI + perf harness added
implementation_notes: Estimate per-request KV bytes using: model.hidden_size * num_layers * 2 (for key+value) * sizeof(float16/qt) * estimated_context_length. Use live histogram of response lengths to refine estimate multiplier.
Batching policy: target per-GPU KV footprint window (e.g., 6GB) and greedily pack requests until estimated footprint >= window or latency budget reached.
Soft slot allocation: allocate logical slots for KV in a slab allocator; prefer packing similarly sized slots to reduce fragmentation.
Compaction: implement lightweight background compaction between micro-batches on the same stream (memcpy-based defragmentation) with throttling so it doesn't increase p95 latency.
Eviction heuristic: when predicted KV oversubscribe, try re-splitting longest-running generation to other GPUs via async offload or apply early-fallback to smaller-quantized model variant.
Integration with batching estimator: add a cost function that blends sequence length, estimated response tokens, and known long-running conditional probability mass to predict KV longevity.
Memory safety: reserve headroom per GPU (configurable percentage) before admitting a batch; expose config for Dedicated customers to tweak safety margin.
Telemetry: new metrics kv_estimated_bytes, kv_allocated_bytes, kv_free_gap_bytes, kv_compaction_ops, batch_pack_efficiency, per_batch_slot_count. Export per-model and per-customer tags.
Config flags: runtime.enable_hybrid_token_batcher, runtime.kv_compaction_enabled, runtime.kv_headroom_pct, runtime.batch_target_kv_bytes
Backward compatibility: keep existing continuous batcher as fallback; implement canary rollout path in console and API (model-level toggle).
tradeoffs: Pros: better effective GPU utilization for mixed workloads, fewer OOMs, and higher sustained throughput on heavy-tail traffic.
Cons: increased scheduler complexity and slightly higher CPU overhead for estimating footprints and compaction bookkeeping.
Compaction cost: aggressive compaction reduces fragmentation but may increase p95 if done synchronously — we choose background, throttled compaction to balance.
Accuracy vs latency: conservative overestimation of KV size reduces OOMs but lowers packing efficiency; tuned multiplier needed per-customer/profile.
Operational complexity: exposes new knobs customers may need to tune for edge cases (very-large-context models or highly bursty traffic).
testing_plan: Unit tests for KV estimator correctness across model dims and quantization profiles.
Microbench harness that replays 10k production trace samples with mixed prompt/response lengths; measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/s, kv_free_gap_bytes.
Load test on Dedicated pool (staging) with long-tail synthetic traces to validate no OOMs and throughput improvements.
A/B canary in hosted environment: 1% users -> 10% -> 50% with automated rollback on latency or error regressions.
Chaos test: inject slow network and CPU to ensure compaction/backpressure behave correctly and do not cascade failures.
Add perf regression gate in CI that fails PRs when packing efficiency drops below the established baseline by >5%.
rollout_plan: Feature behind runtime flag; deploy scheduler binary to staging with kv_compaction disabled by default.
Enable kv_estimator and batch packing in staging; run full trace replay and validate metrics.
Canary rollout in production per region: start 1% traffic for non-enterprise customers, monitor metrics for 72h.
If stable, expand to Dedicated pools and enterprise customers with controlled config exposure in Console.
Post-rollout: run a 2-week observability sweep, collect customer feedback, then promote to default in runtime-2.3.0 if no issues.
